dedupe_keys.name: multi agent deep reinforcement learning routing simulator for leo satellite networks

description: This open-source Python simulator models packet routing in low Earth orbit satellite constellations while accounting for the changing topology and other uncertainties, and was described in a 2024 arXiv paper by Federico Lozano-Cuadra and colleagues. It uses an event-based approach built on the SimPy library to simulate packet creation, routing and queuing, tracking queues and latency as the simulation runs. Routing can follow a traditional Dijkstra shortest path, Q-routing, or multi-agent deep reinforcement learning in which each satellite learns its own forwarding decisions, and the paper reports clear reductions in end-to-end latency with the learning-based policies. Users can change routing policies, traffic, ground and space topologies, link parameters and learning hyperparameters, and can visualise satellite motion and packet paths; constellations such as Kepler, Starlink, OneWeb and Iridium NEXT are configured. Coverage: generic constellations with ground gateways worldwide. Licence: not stated for the software; the describing arXiv preprint is under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Access is free of charge. Caveats: simplified physical layer and traffic; results depend on the learning set-up. Simulation uses: agent-based routing and congestion studies, and resilience of satellite backhaul to node or link failures. Related records: StarPerf and Hypatia model mega-constellation networks, and OpenSN emulates them.
